title: The last N log lines
description:
Build `RecentLog`, which keeps only the most recent log lines in a fixed amount of memory, overwriting the oldest when full.

- The constructor receives the capacity (at least 1).
- `add(line)` stores a line. When the log is full, the oldest line is dropped.
- `lines()` returns the stored lines, **oldest first**.
- `size()` returns how many lines are stored; `dropped()` how many have been overwritten so far.

Store the lines in a `std::vector<std::string>` of exactly `capacity` slots, used as a ring: keep the index where the next line goes and wrap it round to 0 at the end. Do not erase from the front of a vector.

```
RecentLog log{ 3 };
add "a", "b", "c", "d"   ->  lines() = { "b", "c", "d" }, dropped() = 1
```
hints: Keep three counters: where the next line goes, how many lines are stored, and how many have been dropped. After writing a line, move the "next" index on by one and wrap it with `% capacity`.
The oldest stored line is `count` slots before "next", wrapping round: `(next + capacity - count) % capacity`. Read `count` lines from there, wrapping as you go.
rules: Use the vector as a ring: overwrite the oldest slot instead of removing from the front.

rules.message: Use the vector as a ring: overwrite the oldest slot instead of removing from the front.
